details:
Project Details – BeyondOrbit

BeyondOrbit is an interactive space mission design and exploration platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It brings together orbital mechanics, spacecraft systems, planetary environments, and scientific datasets to create an engaging space exploration experience.

What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

BeyondOrbit combines scientific models and publicly available NASA/JPL resources to represent important aspects of space missions. It incorporates orbital dynamics, spacecraft payload capacities, launch vehicle performance, power decay curves, communication budgets, planetary ephemerides, and celestial body information.

The platform uses preprocessed and locally stored scientific datasets to power its simulations. Its offline-first architecture minimizes dependency on external services and runtime API calls.

Benefits and Intended Impact

BeyondOrbit makes complex space science and mission-planning concepts more accessible and engaging. It encourages users to understand the scientific and engineering considerations involved in space exploration, including orbital behaviour, spacecraft limitations, planetary environments, and communication constraints.

Creativity and Innovation

The project combines multiple scientific data sources into one unified interactive experience. It brings together planetary models, star catalogues, spacecraft 3D assets, planetary surface maps, and mission-related parameters. Simplified scientific models make complex concepts easier to explore while retaining connections to real scientific references.

Technologies and Resources

The project uses NASA/JPL scientific resources, JPL Horizons, the Small-Body Database, NASA 3D Resources, the HYG Star Catalog, and Solar System Scope textures. Scientific parameters and simplified models are documented in the project's data provenance records.

Overall Vision

BeyondOrbit aims to inspire curiosity about the universe and demonstrate how real scientific data can be transformed into an accessible, interactive space exploration and mission-design experience.
